title: FPP pluginInfo.json
description: Metadata file every FPP plugin ships in its repository root. Prose reference: PLUGININFO_FORMAT.md in this repo. Strictly validated: every field below is the complete recognized set, including 'version'/'requires' (legacy, ignored by FPP at runtime but explicitly allowed here so a plugin that still carries them from an older template doesn't fail validation) -- anything else is rejected.

repoName.description: Unique identifier and on-disk install directory name. Keep it filesystem/shell safe. Must match the name in fpp-data/pluginList.json.

name.description: Human-readable title shown on the plugin card.

description.description: Short description shown on the plugin card.

homeURL.description: Project home page; rendered as the home link.

srcURL.description: Git clone URL (normally ending in .git). FPP clones this to install. Must be a github.com repo -- that's the only source FPP plugins support, and this is the trust anchor for the Official badge.

bugURL.description: Issue tracker URL; rendered as Report a Bug.

iconURL.description: Icon URL. FPP prefers a local icon.png (128x128 or 256x256) in the repo root and falls back to this, which must be an https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ URL ending in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif or .webp; anything else is ignored.

allowUpdates.description: 0 hides in-place update buttons (install-once plugins). Omitted = allowed. Can be overridden per version.

minMemoryMB.description: Minimum system RAM (MB), plugin-wide (top level only; not read from versions[] entries). Below this, FPP flags the plugin and hides it on the Basic UI level.

minCpuCores.description: Minimum recommended CPU cores, plugin-wide (top level only; not read from versions[] entries). Below this, FPP flags the plugin and hides it on the Basic UI level.

private.description: true if hosted in a private GitHub repo; installed with the credentials on the Developer settings page.

linkName.description: Legacy: creates a symlink on install. Only takes effect when the cloned repo does NOT ship its own pluginInfo.json. New plugins rarely need it.

delist.description: Set true to request removal from FPP's Plugin Manager list (retire the plugin). Because setting it requires write access to your repo, it also serves as proof of ownership for a de-list request. Existing installs are unaffected.

versions.description: Compatibility entries. FPP installs the LAST entry whose FPP-version range and platform match the device, so list them oldest-first.

dependencies.description: Things installed automatically BEFORE the plugin's own scripts/fpp_install.sh (FPP 10+). Applies to every entry in versions[]. A versions[] entry may also declare its own 'dependencies' (see versionEntry) with items ADDITIONAL to this top-level set for that entry only -- e.g. a package name that differs between the FPP9 and FPP10 image.

documentation.description: Optional URL to human documentation for this plugin (e.g. a guide/README elsewhere). Purely informational -- not read or rendered by FPP itself.

version.description: IGNORED. FPP does not read a top-level 'version' -- use versions[] entries for compatibility instead. Allowed here only so a plugin carrying it from an older template doesn't fail validation; don't add it to a new plugin.

requires.description: IGNORED. FPP does not read a top-level 'requires' -- declare needs in the 'dependencies' block instead. Allowed here only so a plugin carrying it from an older template doesn't fail validation; don't add it to a new plugin.

privacy.description: Privacy disclosure (the `privacy` section of PLUGININFO_FORMAT.md; rules in PLUGIN_GUIDELINES.md §14). Optional in the schema but required for listing: a plugin without it cannot be listed or updated (lint_plugin.py's privacy-missing blocker). All eight keys are required and may be empty - an empty array is a statement ("sends nothing"), a missing key fails validation. Self-declared: the listing check greps the plugin's code against it (lint_plugin.py's privacy-undeclared-* rules) and fails on a contradiction. FPP computes the six install-dialog lights from it; the author never picks a colour. See PLUGIN_GUIDELINES.md §14.

platform.description: Must exactly match the value FPP writes to /etc/fpp/platform.

minFPPVersion.description: Minimum FPP version this entry supports, e.g. "9.0".

maxFPPVersion.description: Maximum FPP version. "0", "0.0" or "" mean open-ended, but only within the major named by minFPPVersion; on a newer major the entry is treated as untested.

branch.description: Git branch to check out for this entry.

sha.description: Commit to pin to. "" installs the latest commit on branch.

allowUpdates.description: Per-version override of the top-level allowUpdates.

platforms.description: Restrict this entry to specific hardware. Omit to match all platforms.

dependencies.description: Dependencies ADDITIONAL to the top-level dependencies block, installed only when THIS entry is the one selected for the running FPP version/platform (FPP 10+).
Resolved in order: packages -> python -> scripts -> plugins.

packages.description: System (apt) packages. Reference-counted per requester. Needs a Debian-family platform.

python.description: Python (PyPI) packages, installed via `pip install --break-system-packages` into FPP's system Python (not isolated per plugin, not reference-counted). pip ships by default with FPP.

plugins.description: Other FPP plugins by repoName. Each must exist in fpp-data/pluginList.json.

privacy.description: What the plugin sends, collects, senses, opens to the outside and changes on the host. Eight keys, all required. Written for a neighbour, not a developer: "your phone number and message", not "MSISDN and body". Any other key is rejected here and ignored by FPP.

summary.description: One or two plain sentences for the install dialog: what leaves the device, to whom, and why. 1-200 characters; the listing check warns (never blocks) over 200.

sends.description: Every destination the plugin's traffic reaches off this device - directly, through FPP's helpers (CurlManager, urlGet, core MQTT, MultiSync), from the operator's browser (CDN, fonts, embeds) or from a visitor's device - and every broadcast (FM, LoRa). Empty means the plugin sends nothing.

collects.description: Data the plugin keeps about people. Empty means nothing beyond the operator's own settings.

sensors.description: Cameras, microphones and other sensors the plugin reads. Empty means none. A camera stream that leaves the device is also a `sends` entry.

remoteAccess.description: The plugin's OWN listener, at its widest reach: `none` (nothing, or only routes on FPP's web server), `lan` (a port on the local network), `internet-authenticated` / `internet-open` (a port meant to be reached from the internet, with / without a login), `exposes-fpp` (puts FPP's own pages on the internet), `tunnel` (bundles a tunnel or overlay network that lets an outside service reach this device).

systemChanges.description: Every change outside the plugin's own directory. Empty means nothing outside its own directory.

closedCode.description: true if anything that runs is not in the repository and not from a public package source (apt, pip, npm, CPAN or similar): a prebuilt binary, a downloaded .so, a vendor installer, an obfuscated script.

other.description: Anything the keys above cannot say - what is left behind after uninstall, a visitor-facing page hosted by a vendor, payments taken. "none" if nothing.

to.description: A hostname ("api.twilio.com"; a bare domain covers its subdomains); or a phrase for an operator-entered address ("your MQTT broker", "the FPP players you list"); or a broadcast ("anyone in FM range"). Starts with "http://" when the connection is unencrypted. GitHub hosts (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, *.github.io) are never listed here: fetching code, releases, update checks or a package from GitHub is traffic FPP's plugin manager already makes; a downloaded program is a systemChanges entry of kind download.

what.description: What is sent, in words. Say "CPU serial number" / "MAC address" if a hardware identifier is sent. 1-100 characters (the listing check warns over 100).

why.description: Purpose, in words. 1-100 characters (the listing check warns over 100).

alwaysOn.description: true if it sends before the operator turns anything on (at install, at boot, while fppd runs).

what.description: What is kept, in words. 1-100 characters (the listing check warns over 100).

about.description: Whom it is about. `operator` is the FPP owner; `household` people at the property; `visitors` people who interact with the show; `passers-by` people captured without interacting (camera, presence); `third-parties` people in content (messages, contacts); `performers`.

keptDays.description: How long it is kept, in days. null = kept until deleted by hand.

canDelete.description: true if a control in the plugin's UI deletes it.

where.description: Path under /home/fpp/media/ ("plugindata/fpp-x/", "config/plugin.fpp-x"), or "plugin log". Feeds the crash-bundle exclusion and the backup page.

stored.description: true if frames, audio or detections are written to disk.

kind.description: `service` (units, daemons, cron, mounts, shares) · `network` (a LAN port, mDNS, a port-forward instruction) · `core-settings` (writes FPP's own files or settings) · `download` (extra software fetched at install, a self-update, a runtime download) · `package-source` (an apt/pip/npm source added) · `tunnel` (overlay network, remote-access tunnel) · `reads-core-credentials` (reads FPP's own passwords or tokens) · `privilege` (sudoers, groups, kernel modules, keys on other hosts).

what.description: One line: "enables smbd", "adds fpp to the video group", "downloads the Piper voice models from huggingface.co". Name the host of a download or package source so the listing check can match it. 1-120 characters (the listing check warns over 120).
